Do you like fine food... good hotels
low prices?
This is the year to
Sky-tour
Dine on a sun-drenched patio in Buenos Aires. Order
the finest cuts of beef. Save vour menus to show friends at
home how little it costs to cat to vour heart's content in the
Paris of South America. Be sure to see the smart shops.
Shop for silver in Lima. You'll discover low-priced treas-
ures! This city, called "The fairest gem of the Pacific," was
settled by Spanish Grandees a century before the Pilgrims
landed at Plymouth. It's rich in old Spanish architecture.
Near-by a 2.000-vear-old temple has just been unearthed!
Only Pan American and Panagra can take you
straight down one coast-back the other!
You'll fly from city to city with the greatest
of ease in modern 4-engine Douglas aircraft-
12,000 unduplicated miles. And you'll never be
more than a day away from the U.S.A.
PORT OF SPAIN
• Want to discover some of the world's truly great
vacation lands? Like to be able to go when you
want to go and stay where you want to stay? Un-
crowded South America is the answer-and this
year, smart people are vacationing there.
Now, you can skytour both coasts of South
America by giant DC-6. Fly the East Coast from
New York to Buenos Aires on Pan American's new
Douglas-built "Super-6" Clippers" They're pres-
surized, air-conditioned; offer multi-course con-
tinental dinners with wine; wide, roomy berths.
Fly the West Coast from Buenos Aires to Miami
You never retrace your steps
when you fly down one coast
and back the other. You see
one colorful city after another.
And English is spoken everywhere.
on deluxe El Inter Americano. It's the only daily
DC-6 and the "Fiesta Lounge" flight is the fast-
est U.S. commercial airliner to South America. A
red carpet is rolled out for El Inter Americano.
Stop over wherever you like. One ticket takes
you all the way 'round over the routes of Panagra
and Pan American.
First-class, round-trip fare
from New York is $988.20. Nominal charge for
berths. There's also pressurized tourist service on
both coasts. For reservations, call your Travel
Agent or Pan American.
